full_judgment:
2. The suit was contested by the defendants denying the material facts. According to the defendants the suit land belonged to ex-landlord in khas. Although it was previously in the nature of khal and was recorded in the C.S. khatian as khal, it became cultivable in course of time by gradual accumulation of sands. The landlord possessed the same through bargadars. Thereafter, the Government stepped into the shoes of ex-landlords and by virtue of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act settled the same in favor of one Md. Insan Sheikh. Insan possessed the same on the strength of settlement obtained from the Government. He thereafter sold the suit land to one Daud Hossain who in turn sold the same to the defendant in 1967 by a registered kabala. The defendants have been possessing the same by growing crops on the strength of the aforesaid purchase. According to the defendants, plaintiffs never used the suit land as a public pathway and they acquired no right of easement over the same. 

 8. For the reason stated above there is no substance in the appeal which fails not on the grounds found by the Courts below but in view of the non-compliance of the statutory requirement as indicated above Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, I make no order as to costs.
